info.name: Hardware ERP - Module 1 - Authentication & User Management
info.description:
Module 1 of the Hardware ERP: authentication, users, roles, permissions and the security audit log.

## Before you start

1. Start PostgreSQL: `docker compose up -d`
2. Start the backend: `cd backend && ./mvnw spring-boot:run`
3. Import `hardware-erp-module-01.postman_environment.json` and select it in the environment dropdown (top right).
4. Run **1. Authentication > Login as OWNER**. Every other request uses the token it stores.

## How the tokens work

The **access token** comes back in the response body and is saved to the `accessToken` collection variable by a test script.

The **refresh token** is never in the body. The backend sets it as an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to `/api/v1/auth`. Postman's cookie jar stores and replays it automatically, so `POST /v1/auth/refresh` works with an empty body.

## Running everything at once

Use the Collection Runner in folder order 1 to 6. Folder 5 asserts rejections: a 200 there is a failure, not a success.

## Seed credentials (development only)

| Role | Identifier | Password |
|---|---|---|
| OWNER | 9876543210 | Owner@2026 |
| MANAGER | 9840112233 | Manager@2026 |
| ACCOUNTANT | 9840223344 | Account@2026 |
| STAFF | 9843012345 | Staff@2026 |

These exist only in `db/seed/V900__seed_dev_data.sql`, which the production Flyway configuration does not load.

item.name: 6. Rate Limiting
item.description: The dev profile relaxes the limits so manual testing is not throttled (100/min per IP on login). To see a 429, start the backend with the default profile: `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=default ./mvnw spring-boot:run`, which allows 10 logins per minute per IP and 3 forgot-password requests per hour.
